summary: 80-ft steel tower on Fleetwood Point in the 1930s; the Alexander page gives 1942 as an abandonment date; a 2026 trip report found only a collapsed hut on the summit.

facts.status_note: Tower gone. A 2026 trip report found a collapsed hut on the summit and no tower.

access.note: The 2026 trip report reached the summit on national forest trails. It describes no closure.

visit.trail_note: No tower remains to climb. The trip report followed FT-270, a forestry trail, west from Alexander Mountain and found no obvious trailhead where the trail meets the forest road.

events.note: The Alexander Mountain page gives 1942 as an abandonment date, in the entry right after the tower line. It does not say whether the tower or the station is meant.

evidence.supports: Index lists Fleetwood Point in Lincoln County
Index names Kootenai National Forest as the agency
Index describes Fleetwood Point as a patrol cabin and crow's nest, with no tower
The Alexander Mountain page covers the Alexander Mountain lookout station
80-foot steel tower atop Fleetwood Point, 1.25 miles northwest, in the 1930s
evidence.quote: 1930s: 80' steel tower 1.25 miles northwest atop Fleetwood Point.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The index lists a patrol cabin and crow's nest for Fleetwood Point and mentions no tower. The Alexander page and the 2026 trip report both describe a tower there. The story follows the two tower accounts and says the index differs.

notes_for_editor: No build year is given; the Alexander page says only 1930s, so no built event is recorded. The 1942 abandonment may refer to the station rather than the tower. The trip report also says a tower stood on the Alexander summit, with concrete blocks left; the Alexander page places the 80-ft tower on Fleetwood Point and lists no tower on Alexander Mountain. This is unresolved. The firelookout.org Lincoln County list (Alexander Mountain: Tower Gone) has no Fleetwood entry in the part checked. Only one 2026 personal trip report describes today's site.
